newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.2 pct in March - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.2 pct in March - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.2 percent through the fifth and final week of fiscal March versus February, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.
The index rose 7.7 percent compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales rose 5.4 percent in the week ended April 5 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.

A seasonal softness in Easter week sales coupled with difficult comparisons with Easter sales last year attributed to the week's sluggish performance, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research.

"We knew that it would be a difficult comparison. However, I think it was below expectations even though it was a difficult comparison," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Additionally, the severe snowstorm in the New England last week had adversely affected business in the Northeast, he said.
"Looking at regions around the country, the Northeast was indeed at the bottom of the list last week," Eilenberg said.
Trends in merchandise remained virtually unchanged, with national and regional department stores continuing to stress improvements in apparel sales, he said.
"We're seeing that apparel business and women's accessory business ... is doing well. Now we've had a good couple of months under our belt to examine this ... that is encouraging," he said.
However, Eilenberg said furniture and appliance sales are not doing as well.
